default: This is the DNSi demo server. It answers prepared questions about DNSi only - there is no AI behind it. Try asking: what is dnsi, how do i use dnsi, does dnsi need an api key, or what tools are available.

what is dnsi.answer: DNSi teaches the internet's directory service (DNS, around since 1983) a new trick: your question travels as a domain name, and the answer comes back as the reply. No app, no login, no HTTP. If a device can look up a name, it can ask.

how do i use dnsi.answer: From a terminal: npx dnsi-ask "your question". That asks a DNSi server over plain DNS. You can also run your own server with npm install -g dnsi, then dnsi-server. Any DNS tool (dig, nslookup) works too.
related: does dnsi need an api key

does dnsi need an api key.answer: You (the asker) never need a key: DNS is open, and this demo server has no AI to pay for. If someone runs a DNSi server backed by a real language model, the operator pays for that and can require a token in the question to keep strangers from spending their budget.

what is a dnsi token.answer: A per-zone password embedded in the question name (like ...t.mytoken.ask.dnsi.dev). A zone that requires a token refuses questions without the right one. It keeps abuse and cost down; it does not encrypt anything.
related: does dnsi need an api key

is this an ai.answer: This particular server is not. It answers a fixed set of prepared questions about DNSi, which is why replies are instant and cost nothing. A DNSi server can also be pointed at any AI provider; this one simply is not.

is there an ai behind this server.answer: No. This is the prepared-answers demo: a fixed set of questions about DNSi, answered without any AI. Every answer here is served from cache rules designed for it.

what tools are available.answer: Four built-in tools answer without any AI: tool.time (current UTC time), tool.uuid (random UUID), tool.echo (repeats your text), and tool.hash (SHA-256 of your text). Example name: tool.time.ask.dnsi.dev.

what can dnsi be used for.answer: Terminal Q&A without a browser; asking questions on networks that block everything except DNS; giving gethostbyname-only devices (printers, PLCs, old firmware) AI answers, a clock, a UUID and a hash; team knowledge boxes; and a sanctioned question channel for sandboxed AI agents.

who can ask the dnsi demo server.answer: Anyone who can resolve DNS: any computer, phone, router or embedded device. That is the point. The server rate-limits per source address and logs nothing about who asked.

who made dnsi.answer: DNSi is an open-source experiment by @Omodaka9375. Code: github.com/Omodaka9375/DNSi - site: dnsi.dev. The npm package is dnsi (zero runtime dependencies, two commands: dnsi-server and dnsi-ask).
